stories.headline: Iran's Pezeshkian apologizes to Gulf states, orders halt to strikes on neighbors

key_facts.fact: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian apologized on state TV on Saturday March 7 'on behalf of Iran to the neighboring countries affected' and said the interim leadership council ordered armed forces to stop targeting neighboring states
key_facts.excerpt: Pezeshkian said that the country's interim leadership council, appointed after the killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei last Saturday, had approved a new directive on responding to military threats... Iranian forces are prohibited from targeting neighbouring states unless an attack against Iran is launched directly from that country's territory.

key_facts.fact: Pezeshkian said armed forces had been operating under 'fire at will' authority since commanders were killed, but that this would now stop
key_facts.excerpt: 'The armed forces have so far acted with a kind of fire at will authority, but they have now been notified that from now on they must not attack neighboring countries or target them with missiles,' he said, adding that he 'apologizes personally' over the matter.

key_facts.fact: The apology triggered immediate backlash from Iranian hardliners; lawmaker Mohammad Manan Raeisi called the remarks 'humiliating' and said the Assembly of Experts should quickly select a new leader
key_facts.excerpt: Mohammad Manan Raeisi, a lawmaker representing Qom, described the remarks as 'humiliating' and said they showed the Assembly of Experts should quickly move to select a new leader.

key_facts.fact: Despite the pledge, air-raid sirens blared in Qatar and Bahrain shortly after Pezeshkian's broadcast, and attacks on Gulf countries continued throughout the day
key_facts.excerpt: Masoud Pezeshkian, the Iranian president, had just apologized on state television on Saturday morning for waves of Iranian missile strikes that hit Gulf states since last week, when air-raid sirens blared in Qatar and Bahrain — warning of further attacks.

key_facts.fact: Hours later, following hardliner criticism, Pezeshkian issued a second statement asserting Iran had not attacked 'friendly and neighboring countries,' omitting any apology
key_facts.excerpt: Hours later, following criticism from Iranian hard-liners, Mr. Pezeshkian issued another statement in which he asserted that Iran had not attacked its 'friendly and neighboring countries' in this war — this time omitting any apology at all.

stories.headline: Iran's Assembly of Experts names Mojtaba Khamenei as new supreme leader

key_facts.fact: Iran's Assembly of Experts chose Mojtaba Khamenei, 56-year-old son of the late Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, as the country's new supreme leader, state media reported
key_facts.excerpt: Mojtaba Khamenei, the second son of the late Iranian supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, has been chosen as his successor.

key_facts.fact: Mojtaba is a mid-ranking cleric who never held elected office but cultivated deep influence within the IRGC and his father's office; his elevation marks the first hereditary succession since the 1979 revolution
key_facts.excerpt: Mojtaba Khamenei's elevation marks the first time since the 1979 Islamic revolution that Iran's supreme leadership has passed from father to son.

key_facts.fact: The 88-member Assembly of Experts, supervised by the 12-member Guardian Council, selected Mojtaba after his father was killed on February 28 during the war's opening strikes
key_facts.excerpt: Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei, the second son of former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, has been named Iran's new supreme leader... Mojtaba Khamenei was selected by Iran's Assembly of Experts, comprised of 88 clerics and supervised by the 12-member Guardian Council.

key_facts.fact: The move could lead to escalation as Trump had already called Mojtaba Khamenei an unacceptable choice as leader
key_facts.excerpt: Move could lead to escalation of war as Donald Trump has already called Mojtaba Khamenei an unacceptable choice.

key_facts.fact: Iranian clerics reported consensus on the successor was reached over the March 7-8 weekend, with the official announcement on Sunday
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian clerics reported consensus had been reached on a successor to Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed on February 28.

stories.headline: Trump launches 'Shield of the Americas' coalition at summit with 12 Latin American leaders

key_facts.fact: Trump hosted leaders from 12 Latin American countries at his Doral golf club near Miami on March 7, signing a proclamation launching the 'Shield of the Americas' regional security coalition
key_facts.excerpt: Trump officially launched the coalition, which includes countries such as El Salvador and Panama, on March 7 at an invite-only summit at his Doral golf club near Miami.

key_facts.fact: Attending leaders included presidents of Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guyana, Honduras, Panama, Paraguay, and Trinidad and Tobago; notably absent were Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia
key_facts.excerpt: In attendance were the leaders of Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guyana, Honduras, Panama, Paraguay, and Trinidad and Tobago. Notably, the leaders of Brazil, Mexico and Colombia were not in attendance.

key_facts.fact: Trump called on participating nations to use their militaries against drug cartels; the initiative focuses on combating cartels, drug trafficking, foreign interference, and illegal migration
key_facts.excerpt: The initiative focuses on combating cartels, drug trafficking, foreign interference, and illegal migration.

key_facts.fact: Former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem debuted as the coalition's special envoy after being demoted from her cabinet position on March 5; Oklahoma Sen. Markwayne Mullin was tapped to replace her at DHS
key_facts.excerpt: Former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem is making her debut as the president's special envoy for the Shield of the Americas... Trump said in a March 5 social media post that he was tapping Oklahoma Sen. Markwayne Mullin to lead the Department of Homeland Security.

key_facts.fact: Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who also serves as national security adviser, led the summit and is widely viewed as architect of the hemispheric strategy
key_facts.excerpt: Leaders of participating nations, including El Salvadorian President Nayib Bukele, are attending the all-day gathering that's being led by Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

stories.headline: US economy unexpectedly sheds 92,000 jobs in February, worst since October shutdown

key_facts.fact: Nonfarm payrolls fell by 92,000 in February, far below the consensus expectation of roughly 50,000 job gains; it was the third time in five months that the economy lost jobs
key_facts.excerpt: Nonfarm payrolls in February fell by 92,000, compared with the estimate for 50,000 and below the downwardly revised January total of 126,000. It was the third time in five months that the economy lost jobs.

key_facts.fact: The unemployment rate rose to 4.4% from 4.3%; labor force participation fell to 62.0%, the lowest since December 2021 outside the pandemic
key_facts.excerpt: The labor force participation rate slipped to 62%, its lowest level since December 2021 outside the pandemic.

key_facts.fact: Healthcare, the primary growth driver in payrolls, shed 28,000 jobs largely due to a Kaiser Permanente strike that sidelined more than 30,000 workers in Hawaii and California
key_facts.excerpt: Health care, the primary growth driver in payrolls, saw a loss of 28,000, due largely to a strike at Kaiser Permanente that sidelined more than 30,000 workers in Hawaii and California.

key_facts.fact: Federal government employment continued to drop, shrinking by 10,000 in February; since October 2024, federal jobs have fallen by 330,000 or 11%
key_facts.excerpt: Employment in the federal government also continued to drop, shrinking by 10,000 last month. Since hitting a peak in October 2024, federal government employment has dropped by 330,000, or 11%.

key_facts.fact: Wages rose more than expected, with average hourly earnings up 0.4% monthly and 3.8% year-over-year, both 0.1 percentage point above forecast
key_facts.excerpt: Wages rose more than expected. Average hourly earnings increased 0.4% for the month and 3.8% from a year ago, both 0.1 percentage point above forecast.

key_facts.fact: Economists said the report combined with surging oil prices from the Iran war created a 'one-two punch' of stagflation risk that complicates the Fed's rate cut path
key_facts.excerpt: Economists saw a downside risk to the labor market from a prolonged war in the Middle East, which is driving up oil prices and causing stock market volatility.

stories.headline: G7 calls emergency finance ministers meeting to discuss oil reserves amid prices breaching $100

key_facts.fact: France announced it would host a video meeting of G7 finance ministers on Monday March 10 to 'review the situation in the Gulf from an economic point of view'
key_facts.excerpt: France will host a video meeting of G7 finance ministers on the Middle East crisis on Monday... The French finance ministry said in a statement the meeting at 1:30 pm (1230 GMT) would 'review the situation in the Gulf from an economic point of view.'

key_facts.fact: French Finance Minister Roland Lescure said he agreed with US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other G7 finance ministers to hold the meeting, saying 'it is obviously essential that we coordinate'
key_facts.excerpt: French finance minister Roland Lescure earlier told Franceinfo radio he had agreed with US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other G7 finance ministers to hold the meeting.

key_facts.fact: The use of strategic oil reserves was being considered; the FT reported G7 would discuss a joint release of emergency oil reserves
key_facts.excerpt: 'The use of strategic reserves is an option being considered,' one French official, granted anonymity.

key_facts.fact: Oil prices surged above $100 a barrel over the weekend, with Brent nearing $120 on Monday, reaching the highest level since Russia's 2022 Ukraine invasion
key_facts.excerpt: G7 nations will hold an emergency meeting on Monday to discuss surging oil prices as crude jumped above $100 a barrel and stock markets slumped over the escalating US-Israeli war with Iran.

key_facts.fact: Qatar's energy minister warned oil could reach $150 per barrel; natural gas increased approximately 40% in one week
key_facts.excerpt: Qatar energy minister says oil could reach $150.

stories.headline: Iran war imperils $300B in Gulf AI spending as drones hit AWS data centers, close both data choke points

key_facts.fact: For the first time in history, both the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea are effectively closed to commercial traffic simultaneously, severing the two main routes for data cables in and out of the Gulf
key_facts.excerpt: For the first time, both the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea are effectively closed to commercial traffic... Seventeen submarine cables pass through the Red Sea alone, carrying the majority of data traffic between Europe, Asia, and Africa.

key_facts.fact: Drones struck three AWS data centers over the weekend — two in UAE and one in Bahrain — marking the first confirmed military attacks on a hyperscale cloud provider; AWS advised customers to 'consider migrating workloads out of the Middle East entirely'
key_facts.excerpt: Drones struck three AWS data centers over weekend—two in UAE, one in Bahrain. AWS advised customers to 'consider migrating workloads out of the Middle East entirely.'

key_facts.fact: The Information reported the Iran war is complicating plans by Gulf nations to spend more than $300 billion on data centers, chips, and other AI investments, crimping a potential funding source for power-hungry tech companies
key_facts.excerpt: The war in Iran is complicating plans by Gulf nations to spend more than $300 billion on data centers, chips and other AI investments, crimping a potential source of funding for power-hungry tech companies.

key_facts.fact: Affected megaprojects include the planned 5-gigawatt Stargate UAE AI campus in Abu Dhabi (largest outside US) and Amazon's $5 billion AI hub commitment in Riyadh with Saudi Arabia's Humain
key_facts.excerpt: Stargate UAE: Planned 5-gigawatt AI campus in Abu Dhabi (largest outside U.S.)... Amazon: $5 billion AI hub commitment in Riyadh with Saudi Arabia's Humain.

key_facts.fact: Network expert Doug Madory of Kentik said 'Closing both choke points simultaneously would be a globally disruptive event... I'm not aware of that ever happening'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Closing both choke points simultaneously would be a globally disruptive event...I'm not aware of that ever happening.' — Doug Madory, Kentik

stories.headline: AI-driven layoffs accelerate: Morgan Stanley cuts 2,500 jobs, Oracle plans thousands more

key_facts.fact: Morgan Stanley is cutting approximately 2,500 jobs, roughly 3% of its global workforce, spanning investment banking, trading, wealth management, and asset management divisions
key_facts.excerpt: Morgan Stanley (NYSE:MS) is cutting about 2,500 jobs, roughly 3% of its global workforce. The reductions span investment banking, trading, wealth management, and asset management teams.

key_facts.fact: Morgan Stanley frames the layoffs as part of a broader push for cost efficiency and greater use of AI and automation, despite reporting record 2025 revenue and profits
key_facts.excerpt: Despite record 2025 revenue and profits, layoffs focus on back-office roles and strategic reallocation to AI-driven growth areas.

key_facts.fact: Oracle is planning to cut thousands of jobs across multiple divisions to handle a cash crunch from its massive AI data center expansion, according to Bloomberg; cuts may come as soon as March
key_facts.excerpt: Oracle will cut thousands of jobs to funnel funds into its major AI data centre expansion efforts, according to Bloomberg. The cuts will affect divisions across the company and may come as soon as this month.

key_facts.fact: The layoffs follow Block's February 27 announcement of 40% workforce cuts (over 4,000 jobs), with CEO Jack Dorsey explicitly citing AI as the driver; critics labeled it 'AI-washing'
key_facts.excerpt: Block more than tripled its employee base between 2019 and 2022, growing from 3,835 to 12,430 workers. The company's stock had fallen 40% since early 2025... Goldman Sachs economists estimate that AI is eliminating only 5,000 to 10,000 jobs per month across all U.S. sectors.

key_facts.fact: Goldman Sachs economists estimate AI is eliminating only 5,000 to 10,000 jobs per month across all US sectors, raising questions about whether companies are using AI as cover for traditional cost-cutting
key_facts.excerpt: Goldman Sachs economists estimate that AI is eliminating only 5,000 to 10,000 jobs per month across all U.S. sectors, hardly enough to justify Block's massive cuts.

stories.headline: Nature Aging study identifies glycolytic metabolite PEP as key protector against age-related inflammation

key_facts.fact: Researchers discovered that phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP), a glycolytic metabolite, acts as an endogenous inhibitor of the cGAS-STING inflammatory pathway, protecting against age-related chronic inflammation
key_facts.excerpt: Here we show that phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP), a glycolytic metabolite, acts as a protective factor against age-related chronic inflammation... PEP acts as an endogenous inhibitor of the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)−stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway.

key_facts.fact: PEP levels follow a biphasic trajectory during aging — initially accumulating then progressively declining; blocking PEP accumulation exacerbates inflammation and accelerates aging in mice
key_facts.excerpt: Longitudinal analyses in mice and humans reveal a biphasic PEP trajectory, characterized by initial accumulation followed by progressive decline. Blocking PEP accumulation exacerbates inflammation and accelerates aging phenotypes.

key_facts.fact: Administering PEP to mice before its natural decline promoted healthy aging, while high PEP levels in aged humans strongly correlated with lower inflammation and healthier traits
key_facts.excerpt: PEP administration before its decline promotes healthy aging in mice. In aged humans, high PEP levels strongly correlate with lower inflammation and healthier traits.

key_facts.fact: A companion Nature Aging commentary described the finding as revealing how 'the eventual collapse of PEP offers a metabolic explanation for the onset of inflammaging and neurodegeneration'
key_facts.excerpt: The biphasic fluctuation of PEP levels during aging — and its eventual collapse — offers a metabolic explanation for the onset of inflammaging and neurodegeneration.

key_facts.fact: The study was published March 6, 2026 in Nature Aging by a team led by Huiyan Li, with cross-validation in both mouse models and human cohorts
key_facts.excerpt: Published: 06 March 2026... The glycolytic metabolite phosphoenolpyruvate restricts cGAS-driven inflammation to promote healthy aging.

stories.headline: Oil posts largest weekly gain in futures history at 35%, Brent hits $92.69 as stagflation fears mount

key_facts.fact: Brent crude surged 8.5% to $92.69/barrel on Friday March 7, briefly topping $94 — its highest since September 2023; WTI jumped 12.2% to $90.90/barrel
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. and global benchmark prices on Friday tallied their largest weekly gains on record.

key_facts.fact: Oil posted a 35% weekly gain, the largest since oil futures trading began in 1983, driven by the Iran war and effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz
key_facts.excerpt: The Iran war sent oil futures surging to historic gains this week, while stocks fell sharply in a worldwide selloff.

key_facts.fact: The S&P 500 fell 1.33%, the Dow dropped 453 points (0.95%), and the Nasdaq sank 1.59% on Friday, capping Wall Street's worst week since October
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. and European equity indexes closed a tumultuous week with losses of more than 1% on Friday.

key_facts.fact: The combination of the negative payrolls report and surging oil created a classic stagflation setup, with the Fed boxed in between cutting rates to support growth and risking higher inflation
key_facts.excerpt: A disappointing payrolls report intensified worries that the U.S. economy could be cooling just as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East push energy costs sharply higher. That mix threatens to box in the Federal Reserve.

key_facts.fact: Traders are now pricing in two Fed rate cuts in 2026 with the first expected as early as April; the FOMC is widely expected to hold rates at its March 17-18 meeting
key_facts.excerpt: Economists also viewed the plunge as payback after a large increase in January payrolls... Economists saw a downside risk to the labor market from a prolonged war in the Middle East.
